solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Last of my shipmates cast adrift are in accord

indicators.note: something cast adrift is set loose and scattered, so the letters are rearranged
the last of a word is its final letter, taken here from the word my

explanation.surface: A sailor sees crewmates set adrift and feels for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of my' gives Y, which joins the letters of SHIPMATES before 'cast adrift' scrambles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in accord with someone is to agree with or support their view, which is a sense of feeling with them.

clue.text: Food store set up in metropolis

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top
in signals that the letters sit inside the word metropolis

explanation.surface: A grocery has been opened in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks OLIS from the end of metropOLIS; 'set up' turns it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm tower or pit used to hold grain or fodder, a storage place for animal feed.

clue.text: Greek character retires after saying most

indicators.note: after places the Greek letter behind the saying

parts.note: a maxim is a saying or proverb

indicators.note: retires means withdraws, moving backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person bows out after a comment, as if wise words were the best one could offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' signals the reversal of the Greek letter; 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The greatest possible amount, the upper limit, is the most there can be.

clue.text: Game move blocked by United cross

indicators.note: blocked by means a letter stands in the middle of the word for move, obstructing it

parts.note: a move is an action, a step taken
U is the usual abbreviation for United in football club names
to cross a river is to bridge it

explanation.surface: A football fan is angry that a play was thwarted by Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocked by' puts U inside ACTION to make AUCTION. It is an old form of the card game bridge in which players bid for the contract.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a card game, a forerunner of contract bridge, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Nudist leader wore clothes to leave

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the letters for wore dress or surround the letter

parts.note: if you wore a coat, you had it on

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here from Nudist

explanation.surface: The head of a naturist group put garments on in order to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' wraps HAD ON round N, the 'leader' of Nudist. 'Clothes' looks like a noun, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something to an heir is to pass it on or bequeath it.

clue.text: Type of spurious fairness

indicators.note: spurious means false, not genuine, so the letters of the word are faked into a new order

explanation.surface: The clue reads like a description of fairness that is fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurious' rearranges FAIRNESS. 'Type' looks like 'a kind of', but here it means printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a printing typeface with no small finishing strokes on the letters, so it is a kind of printer's font.

clue.text: Churl not allowed on loch

indicators.note: on places the second piece after the first in an across entry

parts.note: L is a standard abbreviation for loch, as on Scottish maps
a ball that is out is not allowed, outside the lines

explanation.surface: A boorish person is banned from a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A churl is a rude, boorish person, which is the same as a yob.

clue.text: Oriental craft capsized one mile south of old port

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of puts this piece below the others

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia and a port on the Baltic

indicators.note: capsized means turned upside down, so in this down entry the letters run backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An eastern boat overturned a mile south of an ancient harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns I M into MI, which goes 'south of' O and RIGA. 'Craft' suggests a boat, but here it means a handicraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper folding is a traditional Japanese art, a handicraft from the Far East.

clue.text: Under attack, extremely tough Red Guards scoffed

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters, the two ends of the word tough
guards means surrounds, so the colour holds the other piece inside

parts.note: taken as written
scoffed means ate greedily, eaten

explanation.surface: Chinese Red Guards, very hard men, gobbled food while under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Guards' reads as Mao's militia, but 'Guards' is a container signal acting on the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in danger or menaced by an enemy is being attacked.

clue.text: Left graphic symbol on former reference work

indicators.note: on places the symbol after the word for former in an across entry

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
an icon is a small picture used as a symbol on a screen

explanation.surface: Instructions for placing a picture beside an old entry in a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary or word list is a book people consult for information.

clue.text: I'll be caught by youngster with greater agility

indicators.note: be caught by means held inside the word for youngster

parts.note: a nipper is a small child
I'll is I will, giving the letter I, the one to be caught

explanation.surface: Someone fears being caught by a more nimble child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be caught by' puts I inside NIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy means quick and nimble, so the comparative form describes someone moving more quickly.

clue.text: Tossed pack around a couple of times in planned conflict

parts.note: to pitch is to throw or toss

indicators.note: around means the bundle surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a bale is a large bundle or pack of goods
T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them make TT

explanation.surface: Someone threw a bundle about a few times during a scheduled fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal: the bundle goes round the two time abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a set-piece battle fought on ground chosen in advance, so it is a deliberately arranged fight.

clue.text: Supreme surgeon's work held back by ointment supply

indicators.note: held means the reworked letters contain the reversed piece
supply is the adverb of supple, so the letters bend into a new shape
back means read backwards

parts.note: an op is an operation, the work a surgeon does

explanation.surface: A surgeon's operation is delayed because of the supply of ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' rearranges the ointment letters to OMNITENT, which has 'held' the reversed operation inside it. 'Supply' looks like a noun but is the adverb from 'supple'.
explanation.definitionFit: All-powerful means having supreme authority, like an almighty god.

clue.text: Overseas commander's range

definitions.meaning: a Turkish military commander or chief, a foreign title
a large cast-iron cooking stove, sold under a Swedish-founded brand name

explanation.surface: A foreign general's area of operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a title of Ottoman officers and a brand of kitchen range cooker share the same three letters.

clue.text: Roman Brit's strange aberration

indicators.note: strange means odd or unfamiliar, so the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A Romano-British person behaves oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges ROMAN BRITS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden mental lapse or fit of confusion is an aberration, a moment when the mind goes astray.

clue.text: Military men returned bags of traveller

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers
bags of is informal for lots of, plenty

explanation.surface: Soldiers came back with a wanderer's luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns OR into RO. 'Bags' looks like luggage, but 'bags of' means lots.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romani person belongs to a people traditionally living a wandering life, often called travellers.

clue.text: Slap-up celebration

parts.note: slap-up usually means lavish, as in a slap-up meal, but here it is a slap made with hands raised up high to celebrate

explanation.surface: A lavish party.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people celebrate by slapping their raised palms together, a hand gesture of triumph.

clue.text: Put rubbish in sack

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down
waste is rubbish, refuse

explanation.surface: Instructions for putting refuse into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag for rubbish, but here it is a verb: to plunder a town.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a city is to plunder and devastate it.

clue.text: Fumble, ultimately breaking fancy ceramic dish

indicators.note: breaking means the letter bursts into the middle of the other letters
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters take a decorative new order
ultimately points to the final letter of the word Fumble

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles and breaks an ornate china bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges CERAMIC; 'ultimately' gives E from Fumble, 'breaking' into it to make ICE CREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert is a sweet course served at a meal, a dish.

clue.text: Discharges nameless head, bringing in another

indicators.note: bringing in means the shortened word takes the other headland inside it
nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness
a cape is another headland

explanation.surface: A worker is fired without being named, and another boss is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops N (name) to leave ESS; 'bringing in' then takes the second headland inside. 'Head' looks like a boss, but it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaks of gas or radioactive material from a plant are releases or discharges.

clue.text: Editor replaces first book of scripture suitable for course

indicators.note: replaces first means the editor takes the place of the opening letter of the holy book

parts.note: the Bible is the book of Christian scripture

explanation.surface: A new editor takes over the opening book of the Bible, Genesis, to prepare a study course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces first' swaps the B at the start of BIBLE for ED. 'Course' looks like a course of study, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Food fit to be eaten can be served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: British reportedly flog rubbish north of the border

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the word for flog is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to leather someone is to beat or thrash them

explanation.surface: A newspaper claims that British people are selling trash in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives LETHER, which sounds like LEATHER. 'Flog' looks like selling, but it means thrash. 'North of the border' means in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Scottish word for foolish chatter, nonsense spoken at length.

clue.text: One-time bowler possibly superannuated

parts.note: one-time means former, of old
a bowler is a kind of hat, so possibly marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A retired cricket bowler, possibly put out to grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' points to cricket, but it is the round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of date and no longer fashionable is past it, too old to be useful.

clue.text: Bag almost knocked over another

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the letters are read backwards
almost means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: another bag, such as a suitcase or case

explanation.surface: One bag nearly knocks another one over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CASE, another bag, to CAS, and 'knocked over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, a pouch or cavity in a plant or animal is a bag-like structure.

clue.text: Disheartened, like rich man passed from host to client

parts.note: feeling down is feeling disheartened
a rich person is loaded with money

explanation.surface: A wealthy man is downcast, as if passing between a party host and his customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' and 'client' look like people, but they are a server computer and the user's machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A file copied from a server to a user's computer has been transferred from a network host.

clue.text: Trace a revolutionary word from Robespierre?

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so in this down entry the letters run backwards

parts.note: mot is French for word, and Robespierre was a French revolutionary

explanation.surface: A trace of a word spoken by Robespierre, the French revolutionary leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' signals turning round. The question mark flags Robespierre as a hint that the word is French.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny particle or smallest possible amount is a trace of something.

clue.text: Classical musician to press hard for making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means returning, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to sue for something is to press a claim for it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A classical performer pushes hard for a return to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' reverses SUE H PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this lyre player charmed beasts and the gods of the underworld, a musician of classical legend.

clue.text: Devise case for efficient New World weapon

parts.note: to hatch a plan is to devise it

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, the first and last letters of efficient

explanation.surface: Someone argues for an effective new American weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case for' takes the outer letters E and T of efficient.
explanation.definitionFit: A small axe like the tomahawk was a weapon used by Native Americans.

clue.text: Obscure appeal by maiden

indicators.note: by means beside, the two pieces side by side

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
to appeal is to ask or request

explanation.surface: A young woman makes an unclear plea.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to hide or cover it from view.

clue.text: Cook's equipment, initially damn funny source of rolls

parts.note: a kettle is a kitchen pot for boiling water

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word damn

parts.note: rum means odd or funny-peculiar

explanation.surface: A cook's kit is oddly the place where bread rolls come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' suggests bread, but these are drum rolls. A kettledrum is the timpani.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer plays long rolls on this large copper drum, so it produces them.
